source: The Money Guy Show's 'wealth multiplier': what one dollar invested at a given age becomes by 65, assuming an annual return that starts at 10% at age 20 and falls 0.1 percentage points a year to a floor of 5.5% at 65 — the falling rate standing in for a portfolio that de-risks as retirement nears. Compounded monthly.
confidenceNote: A planning convention, not a forecast. The return path is an assumption chosen by its authors; real returns do not decline on a schedule. Used for 'what a dollar at your age is worth at 65' and 'monthly to reach $1M' style benchmarks (BRIEF §4.1) and for the Skill Stacker's ledger (§7.3), never as an expected return in a projection — engines/projection.js keeps its own single rate.
note: annualReturnAt(age) = max(floorRate, startRate - decayPerYear * (age - startAge)). Multiplier from age a to 65 is the product over each month m of (1 + annualReturnAt(ageAtMonth m) / 12). The engine that reads this computes the curve; nothing here is pre-tabulated so the parameters stay the single source.
